short_title: Brooklyn building collapse: what we know #shorts
short_description:
What we know about the building collapse in Flatbush, Brooklyn (information as of November 12, 2026).

⚠️ Disclaimer: all images in this video are AI-generated illustrations for explanation only. They are NOT real images or footage of the event.

On November 11, 2026, a three-story building on Flatbush Avenue collapsed into an adjacent construction excavation dug for a new residential building. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed that eight people died; at least 17 people were injured, according to officials. The NYC Department of Buildings and law enforcement are investigating; the cause has not been officially determined.

Why excavations next to buildings matter: a building's foundation relies on the soil around it. New York City's Building Code requires whoever performs excavation or foundation work to protect adjoining structures, for example by underpinning their foundations.

If you see new cracks or unsafe conditions in a building near construction in New York City, report them to 311.

Our thoughts are with the victims and their families.

Sources: NYC Mayor's Office and FDNY briefings as reported by ABC7 New York, UPI, Gothamist and CNN (November 11–12, 2026); New York City Building Code, Chapter 33.
